Wizna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ruś, Poland

Not demolished. Wizna's Jewish community, present no later than the 18th century, came under the authority of the larger Tykocin community in 1765, documented elsewhere in this collection, and reached 714 people (26 percent of the town) by 1921, most murdered between June and July 1941. This cemetery, likely founded in the second half of the 18th century, was first documented in an 1781 Catholic parish visitation report describing burial grounds for Jewish children and the poor; victims murdered in summer 1941 are buried there. In 2014, a new private owner's earthmoving work, including burrowing into the hillside, violated and desecrated many graves, scattering bones mixed with sand away from the property.
